answers.answer: Shuffle the Conflict I, II, and III tiers separately. From top to bottom, use 1 randomly dealt card from the 4 Conflict I cards, then 5 randomly dealt cards from the 10 Conflict II cards, then all 4 Conflict III cards in shuffled order. Return all unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘1 card randomly dealt’ from Conflict I; ‘5 cards randomly dealt’ from Conflict II; ‘all 4 Conflict III cards’; unused cards return to the box without looking.

answers.answer: Each human starts with 2 Agents on their Leader and a third (Swordmaster) next to the board. They have 12 troops total: 3 in their garrison and the other 9 in supply. Each starts with 1 water and one cube at the bottom of each of the four Influence tracks. Starting VP is 0 in a three-player game and 1 in a four-player game.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘2 Agents’; third Agent is the Swordmaster; 3 troops in garrison and the rest of the 12 in supply; 1 water; cubes on bottom spaces; Score track on 1 in 4-player, otherwise 0.

answers.answer: Yes. You may take a Reveal turn while Agents remain. Once you have Revealed, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot take another Agent turn. Plot Intrigue can be played only during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns, so you cannot play one later in the phase after Revealing.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Agent turns are optional and you may Reveal with Agents left; after Reveal, your turns are skipped. Plot Intrigue may be played during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up and choose one Agent icon on it matching an icon at the destination; one card sends only one Agent, and a card with no Agent icon cannot be used for an Agent turn. Send one Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied space. Meet the space requirements and pay its costs immediately before resolving any space or card effects; if unable to pay, you cannot send the Agent there.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: ‘play one card’; choose only one matching Agent icon; no Agent icons means Reveal only; space must be unoccupied; costs paid before effects and inability to pay prevents entry.

answers.answer: No. Conspire's 4-spice entry cost must be paid before resolving the played card's Agent box, so gaining spice from that card cannot fund entry when you have only 3 spice. After paying the entry cost, resolve the board-space effect, card Agent box, and one-space Faction Influence advancement in any order.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: costs are paid immediately before any effects; space, Agent box, and Faction advancement resolve in any order afterward. Board-space table: Conspire costs 4 spice.

answers.answer: You may deploy all 3 troops recruited this turn plus up to 2 more from your garrison, for a maximum of 5. Any recruited troops not deployed go to your garrison. Rally Troops normally cannot deploy its recruits because it is not a Combat space; its four recruits go to your garrison.
answers.evidence: Deploying: any or all troops recruited this turn plus ‘up to two more’ from garrison; undeployed recruits go to garrison. Rally Troops is ‘not a Combat space’ and recruits go to garrison.

answers.answer: The four steps are: reveal all remaining hand cards; resolve the Reveal boxes of those newly revealed cards in any order; set Combat strength; clean up. Reveal boxes on cards played earlier during Agent turns are not used. At cleanup, all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn’s four numbered steps; Resolve Reveal Effects specifies cards just revealed, not Agent-turn cards; Clean Up puts all cards in front of you into your discard pile.

answers.answer: Yes, after acquiring a card the Imperium Row refills immediately, so you may buy its replacement if you can afford it. Persuasion from multiple sources may be pooled for one card and Persuasion from one source may be split across cards. Unused Persuasion cannot be saved; it is lost at the end of the Reveal turn. Acquired cards go to the discard pile and cannot be used immediately. An Acquire box resolves once at the moment the card is acquired, not when played.
answers.evidence: Acquiring cards: Persuasion may be pooled or split; row refills immediately; unused Persuasion is lost; acquired cards go to discard and are not used right away; Acquire box resolves at acquisition.

answers.answer: Three troops are worth 6 strength and four revealed swords add 4, for 10 total. If the last deployed troop is removed, strength becomes 0 and cannot be increased by any means, including swords. For strength over 20, flip the Combat marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Each Conflict troop is 2 strength and each revealed sword is 1; no troops means strength 0 regardless of swords; over 20 uses the +20 side of the marker.

answers.answer: During Combat, players with at least one troop in the Conflict may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards or pass. Play proceeds from the First Player clockwise. A pass does not prevent a player from playing again later in the phase. Combat resolves after all players involved pass consecutively. A ‘when you win a Conflict’ card is played only after you have won, before the next phase; if such a card is drawn as a victory reward, it may be played immediately.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue cards: players with a troop act from First Player clockwise; may play any number or pass; prior pass does not bind; resolve after consecutive passes; win-trigger timing is after winning.

answers.answer: A and B do not win; each receives the second reward for the first-place tie. C and D still compete for the third reward, which C receives by beating D (ordinary third-place rewards exist in four-player games). A tie for second gives the third reward to each tied player, including in two- and three-player games; a tie for third gives nothing. A player with 0 strength receives no reward. After rewards, each player's Conflict troops return to their supply, not their garrison.
answers.evidence: Tied first: no winner and tied players receive second reward; in four players the others still compete for third. Tied second: third reward each; tied third: nothing; 0 strength: no reward; troops go to supply.

answers.answer: Normal harvesting occurs when an Agent is sent to a Maker space: Imperial Basin gives 1 base spice, Hagga Basin 2, and The Great Flat 3, plus any accumulated bonus spice. In Phase 4: Makers, after Combat, put 1 spice from the bank on each of those three spaces that has no Agent; bonus spice accumulates across rounds. If an Agent moved away before Makers, the space is empty then, so it receives bonus spice.
answers.evidence: Maker spaces are The Great Flat, Hagga Basin, and Imperial Basin; an Agent-free space gets 1 spice during Makers. FAQ gives base spice values; clarification says a moved-away Agent leaves the space empty for Phase 4 bonus.

answers.answer: Reaching 10 VP mid-round does not end the game immediately; the trigger is checked at the end of the round in Phase 5: Recall. An empty Conflict Deck also triggers the endgame at that check after the last Conflict has been revealed and the round resolves. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigue cards, then most VP wins. Ties are broken by spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops, then the player who most recently took a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Game end is checked at end of a round (Phase 5) for 10+ VP or empty Conflict Deck; Endgame Intrigue resolves first; tiebreak order lists spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, most recent Reveal turn.

answers.answer: The VP for reaching 2 Influence is lost if you drop below 2 and regained when you reach 2 again. The bonus earned at 4 Influence is kept if you later fall below 4 and can be earned again by dropping back and re-advancing. The first player to reach 4 takes the Alliance and its VP; another player takes it by advancing to a higher track space. Merely tying the holder does not take it; if the holder loses Influence while tied, the previously tied player takes it (if several were tied, the holder chooses).
answers.evidence: Faction Influence: 2-Influence VP is lost and regained; 4-Influence bonus is not given back and can be earned again. Alliances: first to 4 takes it; passing the holder to a higher space transfers it; tie alone does not; holder's loss while tied transfers it.

answers.answer: If you lose 1 Influence while tied at 5 with two opponents, one of those tied opponents takes the Alliance; because several were tied, you choose which one. If instead you were the only player at 4 and fall to 3, you lose the Alliance; with no other player at 4 or higher to take it, it returns to the board. The former holder loses the Alliance VP.
answers.evidence: If the holder loses Influence while previously tied, a tied player takes it; if several were tied, holder chooses. Falling to 3 or less loses it; if no player has 4+, it returns to board and former holder loses VP.

answers.answer: A discard instruction means discard a card from your hand unless otherwise specified; it goes to your discard pile. Trashing permanently removes a card from your hand, discard pile, or in play to the game box; a Reserve card returns to its Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or a card directs you to trash itself. You cannot reshuffle early just to inspect a deck: if the deck is empty, you cannot use an ability such as Poison Snooper to look at its top card; reshuffling happens when unable to draw.
answers.evidence: Trashing cards defines discard source/destination and trash eligible locations/destination, including Reserve; optionality exceptions stated. Deck exhaustion says reshuffle when unable to draw and cannot reshuffle early to look at the top card.

answers.answer: Arrakeen's and Carthag's controller gains 1 Solari whenever any player, including the controller, visits; Imperial Basin's controller gains 1 spice on any visit. Winning the matching Conflict lets the winner place a Control marker on that space's flag, replacing an opponent's marker. Later, when a Conflict card is revealed for a space you already control, you may deploy one troop from your supply to the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Control: winning the named Conflict places/replaces the marker; controller receives the listed bonus whenever any player visits; revealing a Conflict for a controlled space permits one troop from supply to deploy.

answers.answer: Use an unused color. Put one Rival cube at the bottom of each of the four Influence tracks and all remaining cubes in its supply; it starts with no troops in its garrison. Remove the three Arrakeen cards marked 1P, shuffle the remaining House Hagal cards, and place the deck and three Agents near its supply. It has no Rival Leader or solo difficulty rules. After each First Player Agent turn, it takes an Agent turn if it has an Agent in supply; it does not act after the other human's turn or after a Reveal turn. It never Reveals, and its Agents return to supply during Recall. It collects no resources, Imperium deck, VP, Conflict rewards, or Control, but it can take and hold Faction Alliances (denying their VP to humans).
answers.evidence: House Hagal Setup and Agent turns specify the unused color, cubes, empty garrison, removed cards, deck and three Agents, turn timing, no Reveal and Recall. Intro specifies no resources/deck/VP/rewards/Control but can hold Alliances.

answers.answer: Reveal House Hagal cards until one indicates an eligible unoccupied space; if a card has two spaces, use only the option matching current conditions, and if that option is occupied draw another card rather than switching options. If its deck is empty or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue revealing. Ignore normal space costs, requirements, and effects; resolve only the card's icons and instructions. Each troop icon recruits from its supply, deploying it if this is a Combat space and otherwise putting it in its garrison. Whenever Hagal sends an Agent to a Combat space, it may also deploy up to two garrison troops, even if the card recruited none. Harvest Spice follows its card instructions; harvested bonus spice is removed from the space and returned to the bank rather than accumulated for Hagal.
answers.evidence: House Hagal turn procedure covers occupied spaces, Reshuffle, applicable option, ignoring normal space rules, troop recruitment/deployment, two additional garrison troops and Harvest Spice treatment.

answers.answer: At the start of Combat, if Hagal has at least one deployed troop, reveal a Hagal card in turn order; if it is Reshuffle, reshuffle and reveal again. Ignore everything except its bottom sword icons and add those to the usual 2 strength per deployed troop. Humans may then play Combat Intrigue before resolution. Hagal receives no reward for its rank but occupies that rank when human rewards are assigned. Ordinary third place pays nothing; human players tied for second each get the third reward even in a two-player game. If Hagal wins a Conflict for a space a human controls, remove that Control marker and Hagal does not replace it. After Combat, troops return to supply and markers reset.
answers.evidence: Combat strength procedure: reveal/reshuffle as needed, swords only plus 2 per deployed troop, then humans may play Combat Intrigue. Hagal section states it gets no reward but occupies rank, tied second pays third reward, and winning a controlled-space Conflict removes the marker; troops return to supply.
